items.title: CVE-2026-47839 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Core IdAM/OIDC federation component in enterprise cloud platforms; bypass grants full admin control over user identities and session tokens.

items.title: CVE-2026-49464 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Government sector: IDOR in Dutch citizen portal backend allows authenticated users to access/modify other citizens' civic task submissions and PII.

items.title: CVE-2026-54072 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Directly compromises OAuth 2.0/OIDC identity providers, enabling full account takeover via token exfiltration in public-facing authentication infrastructure.

items.title: CVE-2026-73784 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: TIER 2 SAML signature bypass in HPE IceWall IAM/SSO gateway enables direct identity takeover, directly impacting Digital Identity infrastructure.

items.title: CVE-2026-78133 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Foundational VPN gateway (strongSwan) underpins secure remote access and site-to-site connectivity for government, enterprise, and regulated sectors.

items.title: CVE-2026-80462 (Tier 2)
items.excerpt: Critical unauthenticated API bypass in Chef Automate, a general infrastructure platform widely deployed to manage CI/CD and automation pipelines for government, finance, and healthcare sectors.

items.title: Inside an AI‑enabled device code phishing campaign
items.excerpt: A new wave of device code phishing shows how threat actors are scaling account compromise using AI and end‑to‑end automation. This campaign goes beyond traditional phishing by generating live authentication codes on demand, enabling higher success rates and sustained post‑compromise access.

items.title: When checking the URL isn’t enough: phishing via the Microsoft identity platform | Securelist
items.excerpt: Kaspersky Securelist examines how threat actors exploit legitimate Microsoft identity platform endpoints to conduct highly convincing phishing campaigns. By leveraging trusted OAuth flows and valid Microsoft domains, attackers evade traditional URL filtering and user suspicion. The analysis provides technical breakdowns of the attack chain, infrastructure patterns, and defensive recommendations for identity protection.

items.title: Device Code Phishing is an Evolution in Identity Takeover - Proofpoint
items.excerpt: Proofpoint analyzes how device code phishing has evolved into a sophisticated identity takeover vector. Attackers now automate credential harvesting and session token theft, bypassing traditional multi-factor authentication. The report details detection strategies, infrastructure indicators, and mitigation controls essential for enterprise security teams defending against modern identity attacks.

items.title: Device Code Phishing: Turning a Convenience Feature Into an MFA Bypass | Trend Micro (US)
items.excerpt: Trend Micro research details how the device code authentication flow, originally designed for keyboard-less devices, is being weaponized to bypass MFA. Attackers trick users into entering codes on malicious sites, granting immediate account access. The article outlines threat actor tactics, infrastructure indicators, and actionable mitigation steps for IT administrators managing enterprise identity environments.

items.title: Laundry Bear Zero-Click Zimbra Phishing Campaign Warned by CISA
items.excerpt: CISA alerts on a zero-click phishing campaign by the Laundry Bear group exploiting a critical Zimbra vulnerability. Attackers deliver malicious payloads without user interaction, compromising email infrastructure across Western government and critical infrastructure sectors. The advisory outlines affected versions, patch guidance, and network monitoring strategies for infrastructure defenders.

items.title: AI-enabled device code phishing campaign exploits OAuth flow for account takeover - Help Net Security
items.excerpt: This report covers a coordinated campaign leveraging AI-generated lures and automated OAuth device code flows to compromise enterprise accounts. Threat actors dynamically generate authentication prompts, significantly increasing success rates. The analysis highlights infrastructure footprints, detection signatures, and policy adjustments required to secure identity platforms against AI-augmented phishing operations.

items.title: Russian hacker group Laundry Bear exploits Zimbra zero-click flaw to target Western government, critical infrastructure
items.excerpt: Industrial Cyber reports on Laundry Bear’s exploitation of a zero-click Zimbra flaw to infiltrate Western government and critical infrastructure networks. The campaign leverages unpatched email servers to deploy backdoors and exfiltrate data. The analysis provides threat intelligence, infrastructure indicators, and remediation steps for IT teams managing legacy or vulnerable email platforms.

items.title: Three Active Microsoft 365 Phishing Campaigns Targeting Schools and Government Agencies
items.excerpt: Forsyte IT identifies three concurrent phishing campaigns specifically targeting educational and government Microsoft 365 tenants. Attackers use tailored lures mimicking internal communications and compliance notices to harvest credentials. The article provides campaign indicators, email header analysis, and configuration hardening steps for IT defenders managing public sector identity infrastructure.

items.title: CVE-2026-57967
items.excerpt:
An unauthenticated remote attacker can craft a CORE protocol SESSION_REATTACH packet to steal an existing session and assume ongoing execution of the previously authenticated session.



This issue affects Apache Artemis: from 2.50.0 through 2.56.0; Apache ActiveMQ Artemis: from 1.0.0 through 2.44.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.57.0, which fixes the issue.

items.title: CVE-2026-82107
items.excerpt: IBM DataStage on Cloud Pak for Data 5.4.0.0 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information and bypass security restrictions due to improper authentication.

items.title: CVE-2026-89042
items.excerpt: passport-saml-encrypted through 0.1.13 makes SAML signature verification conditional on an optional cert option, allowing attackers to bypass authentication by submitting unsigned SAML responses. Attackers can post forged SAML responses with arbitrary NameID and attributes to the assertion consumer service endpoint to receive authenticated profiles without valid signatures.

items.title: CVE-2026-88007
items.excerpt: Traefik is an open source HTTP reverse proxy and load balancer. From 2.11.0 until 2.11.57 and 3.7.13, the HTTP/3 entrypoint ConnContext does not call service.AddTransportOnContext, so kerberosRoundTripper uses a shared backend transport instead of a transport dedicated to each frontend connection. items.title: CVE-2026-89043
items.excerpt: passport-saml-encrypted through 0.1.13 contains an XML signature wrapping vulnerability where signature verification and assertion extraction use independent XPath lookups with no cross-validation. Attackers holding any validly signed SAML message can prepend a forged unsigned assertion that gets accepted as the verified identity while the genuine signature validates against the original assertion.

items.title: CVE-2026-88895
items.excerpt: CyberPanel before 3.0.5 fails to enforce two-factor authentication on API endpoints, allowing attackers to bypass TOTP requirements using password-derived tokens. Attackers who obtain an administrator's password can derive API tokens and perform administrative operations or create authenticated sessions without the second factor.

items.title: CVE-2026-0307
items.excerpt:
Multiple local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in the Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect™ app allows a local user to escalate their privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Windows and root on macOS and Linux. This enables a non-administrative user to execute arbitrary commands with administrative privileges.



This GlobalProtect app on iOS, Android and ChromeOS is not impacted.
